content: {"rule":"K-S2","applies":"yes","applies_why":"The judge text grounds an UNDERDETERMINED label on Matthew 1:16's passive egennēthē not stating a verdict on the begetter in either direction.","verdict":"BREACH","quote":"D1 vs C3 (Matthew 1:16): UNDERDETERMINED -- the passive egennēthē states no verdict on the begetter in either direction, and the defender answered Luke 1:27, Luke 2:4 and Numbers 1:2 in [CR2] section A.3 and [CR3]; the verb change is real [L1]/[L2] but neither text's own words state the other reading's contrary.","rule_words":"That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side.","room":"Phrase 'a single verse does not state a link or its contrary': weighed whether a verse's silence can support UNDERDETERMINED versus whether it can never do so; K-S2 requires the latter.","why":"The judge uses Matthew 1:16's not stating a verdict on the begetter and the absence of contrary words as the reason for UNDERDETERMINED, which K-S2 forbids."}
